Paradox Gain table -- Event: Paradox Dice: every out-of-character act = 1 die; every month you live in a location where you've had a dozen or more known resplendent destinies during the last 10 years = 1 die; character wearing a resplendent destiny causes her anima banner to activate at the 4-7 level = 1 die; ...at the 8-10 level or above = 2 dice; confusing meeting as her Exalted self with someone she's had contact with while wearing a resplendent destiny = 1 die; confusing meeting as another resplendent destiny with someone she's had contact with as a resplendent destiny = 1 die; ...and they conclude she's one resplendent destiny imitating another = 2 dice; ...and they conclude she's a supernatural being = 3 dice. Using Resplendent Powers: Sidereal characters have access to the powers of all their resplendent destinies at all times, even if they are simply being 'themselves' or actively masquerading behind a different resplendent destiny; invoking resplendent powers is generally reflexive unless they allow attacks, in which case they're simple actions. Resplendent powers never generate Paradox for the Exalt even if used in front of large crowds and are out of fate for the destiny -- but they may cause many questions and difficulties -- the pattern spiders will not strike the character down for it. Unlike ascending and descending effects, the powers of resplendent destinies work on creatures outside fate. Note that the character cannot exercise a power in a destiny if she wishes to maintain an identity; if the destiny's effect points are expended or it ends, the identity will dissolve in the Arcane Fate, and a character cannot have two of the same destiny on herself. Wanting, Ceasing and Walking Outside Fate (sidebar): certain Charm effects (Ceasing to Exist Approach, Wanting and Fearing Prayer, Walking Outside Fate) can alter a character's fate dramatically at the same time as a resplendent destiny; where these Charms are in effect at the same time as a resplendent destiny, the Charms' effects take precedence over the Sidereal astrological effect, but do not supersede it. Characters with resplendent destinies are subject to Wanting and Fearing Prayer adopting new station and identity with their resplendent destiny; Sidereals using Ceasing to Exist Approach must choose new identities for their resplendent destinies as well, but don't bother to do so unless the character actually plans to don them. Characters who are Walking Outside Fate cannot invoke any resplendent destiny powers while they are, for that time, walking outside of fate; while they have no destiny, the resplendent destinies do not disappear, they are merely inaccessible.
cost: 1 Willpower and a turn to don/end a resplendent identity; Paradox risk per the Paradox Gain table (out-of-character acts, anima banner triggers at 4-7/8-10+, confused identity meetings).
compatibility: All Sidereal castes; requires initiation in the college whose destiny is assumed; interacts with (but does not supersede) Ceasing to Exist Approach, Wanting and Fearing Prayer, and Walking Outside Fate.
notes: 'Resplendent Destinies' section in full: intro, 'Changing What You Are,' 'Being What You Aren't,' 'Resplendency Paradox' (with its Paradox Gain table), and 'Using Resplendent Powers,' printed pp. 215-217 (PDF 218-220). The 'Wanting, Ceasing and Walking Outside Fate' sidebar (printed p. 216/PDF 219) is folded into this row's mechanics rather than split out, since it is a short cross-reference note about specific Charms' interaction with this same system rather than a separate mechanic. This closes out the resplendent-destinies system flagged as out-of-scope in arcane-fate-anima-banner-visibility-table's notes.

name: Procedure for Sidereal Astrology and Catalog of Colleges (overview)
summary: A condensed, quick-reference restatement of the full astrology procedure (optional pre-rolls, then the Prayer Roll and Effect Roll with all their modifiers) immediately precedes the Catalog of Colleges, which then lists the 25 constellations of the Exalted horoscope grouped into five houses (one per Maiden), each controlled by a college of pattern spiders with its own trappings, correlations and three named resplendent effects; mortals can learn a college's trappings/effects through Occult study but cannot work the astrology themselves, since the spiders answer only to Sidereal priests.
requirements: n/a (reference/overview row); the underlying rolls are covered by sidereal-astrology-petitions and sidereal-astrology-effect-roll.
mechanics: Procedure for Sidereal Astrology (condensed steps): (Optional) Plan Destinies -- roll Intelligence + Craft (Fate) with difficulty equal to the highest Essence of anyone to be directly affected by the invocation; Charms may apply to this roll, to a maximum of the character's Essence; requires one day of planning. (Optional) Compute Horoscopes -- roll Intelligence + Occult, difficulty 1, but the character cannot apply more successes than his destiny planning; requires one day of observation. (Optional) Ritual Behavior -- by bearing the trappings of the constellation for three full days before invoking the effect, the character can add one die to the effect test; a character who instead dons the resplendent destiny for the constellation gains three dice. Prayer Roll -- the Sidereal's player rolls Charisma + Performance, difficulty 6 (5 if it is one of the five colleges of his Maiden's astrological house). If the prayer fails, add destinies and horoscopes produced for it are ruined. Add 2 difficulty to the prayer roll if the character doesn't have a petition. Prayer Roll Modifiers: Create Petition -- roll Wits + Linguistics or Wits + Craft (Calligraphy) at difficulty 2; add 2 difficulty for drawing up the petition in a single turn; four or more additional successes subtract 2 from the difficulty of the prayer roll, four or more additional successes subtract 4 (see sidereal-astrology-petitions for the full breakdown). Cosignatures -- other Sidereals can sign the petition if authorized (see sidereal-astrology-petitions); each cosignatory's player must succeed at a difficulty 1 Wits + Linguistics or Wits + Craft (Calligraphy) roll; each cosignatory adds one die to the prayer roll. Countersignatures -- the god controlling the division of the college may also sign off; this requires a separate prayer and sacrifice, and characters praying for countersignatures are considered priests if they are praying to the head of their division; the signature adds three dice to the prayer roll. Lengthy Prayers -- add one die per three full hours of ritual, to a maximum of +3 dice. Stunts -- well-described rolls add one to three dice as normal; these stunts also often qualify as ritual behavior. Effect Roll -- the character spends a temporary Willpower, and his player rolls the Sidereal's Essence + College, plus any bonuses accumulated from planning, drawing horoscope, and ritual behavior. All effect adders stack with all other effect adders. Excellent Petition -- +1 effect die per additional three successes on the prayer roll. Preplanned Fate -- +1 effect die per additional three successes on the Craft (Fate) roll. Precomputed Horoscopes -- +1 effect die per additional three successes on the Occult roll. Ritual Behavior -- add one effect die if the effect bears at least three trappings for three days; add three dice if the character dons the resplendent destiny in question during that time; add one additional die if the target already resides in the precincts of the college. Multiple Sidereals -- add each Sidereal's Essence to the effect roll; all additional Sidereal participants must be legal cosignatories of the petition. Choose Effect -- must touch the target to activate it. Consult the Catalog of Colleges and the tables in this section for the effect. Sidereals must affect each being with Essence greater than 1 individually. Remember the effect doesn't work on other Sidereals and beings outside fate. Paradox Roll -- roll one die for invoking Sidereal astrology at all, plus one additional die per point of Paradox already accumulated (see sidereal-astrology-paradox). Catalog of Colleges (overview): the following are the 25 constellations of the Exalted horoscope. Each is controlled by a college of pattern spiders, and each is predisposed toward sorts of fates and destinies. These predispositions are not merely mythology or speculation in a book of horoscope, but details of the actual division of responsibilities among heavenly bureaus. At the same time, keep in mind that responsibilities among pattern spiders have more to do with the texture and tone of the Tapestry than any single objective measure. While the spiders are actual creatures, they are strange and difficult for human logic to understand. This is a guide, not an exhaustive reference; characters may justify unlikely effects through esoteric logic, or find that intuitive solutions are more difficult to justify than they appear. 'What Do Mortals Know?' sidebar: mortals know the names of the constellations and the images and astrological houses associated with them; those with Occult 1 know the trappings associated with them and may use them to attempt astrological magic, though this is ineffectual since the spiders only listen to Sidereal prayers; mortals know a fair amount about the constellations' purviews and effects but nothing at all about the Loom of Fate, the Bureau of Destiny, or the Sidereal Exalted.
cost: n/a (procedural summary; see the individual rolls it recaps for their own costs).
compatibility: All Sidereal castes; the base prayer difficulty of 5 (rather than 6) applies only to colleges within the Sidereal's own patron Maiden's house.
notes: 'Procedure for Sidereal Astrology' (printed pp. 218-219/PDF 221-222) is a condensed quick-reference version of the same rolls already detailed discursively in sidereal-astrology-petitions and sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; it is captured here as a single overview row (rather than re-split into the earlier rows) so the Catalog of Colleges' own immediate lead-in ('Catalog of Colleges' header and 'What Do Mortals Know?' sidebar, printed pp. 219-220/PDF 222-223) stays attached to its context. The 25 individual colleges themselves are inventoried in five per-house rows (sidereal-astrology-house-of-journeys/serenity/battles/secrets/endings).

name: Open the Spirit Door
summary: Terrestrial Circle spell that lets the caster physically bring herself and companions into the sanctum of a spirit with an Essence equal to or lower than her own, and can also be used to reach the Celestial City of Yu-Shan.
requirements: Prerequisite Charm: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery.
mechanics: This spell allows the caster and anyone she cares to bring with her to physically enter the sanctum of any spirit with an Essence equal to or lower than the caster's. The caster can also use this spell to enter the sanctums of more powerful spirits, but only with the owner's permission. This spell allows the caster to dematerialize, cast it to enter a small god's sanctum, and rematerialize when she leaves the sanctum. To cast this spell the caster and everyone she is bringing along with her must be within three yards of the sanctum's entrance. To locate a sanctum, the sorcerer's player can either ask a spirit, use the Spirit Detecting Glance Charm, or perform a complex divination requiring several hours and a Perception + Occult roll of difficulty 3. If the sorcerer's player succeeds on this roll, the Exalt has located all sanctum entrances within a 100-yard radius. Once the entrance has been found, the caster and her companions need only stand before it and cast this spell. In the next instant, they find themselves physically on the threshold of the sanctum, and for the duration of the spell everyone under its influence can interact physically with the sanctum, its inhabitants and furnishings. This spell lasts until the sun next crosses the horizon. If the caster wishes to leave the sanctum before the duration of the spell is up, she can simply cast the spell again, and she and everyone she brings with her will find themselves back in the mortal world; regardless of how the caster and her companions leave the sanctum, they always find themselves back in the exact place where the spell was first cast. Anyone using this spell can carry items and other furnishings out of the sanctum so long as she can pick them up and carry them. Spirits generally strongly object to having their sanctums invaded by greedy or aggressive Exalted, and anyone who makes a habit of attacking the sanctums of small gods will eventually have to deal with the wrath of more powerful spirits who object to their underlings being harmed or robbed. This spell can also be used to gain admittance to the Celestial City of Yu-Shan, though anyone attempting to enter Yu-Shan this way must talk their way past the celestial lions who guard it (see pp. 18-19 of this book for more on entering Yu-Shan). While a number of clever Exalted have used this spell as a method of hiding from mundane pursuit, it cannot be used to intangibly move through space.
cost: 15 motes, plus 5 motes per additional target brought along.
compatibility: Any Sidereal Exalted who has learned Terrestrial Circle Sorcery; per the Terrestrial Circle Sorcery Charm's notes, almost no Solars, and no Lunars or Abyssals, can learn or cast this spell, though it is not unique to Sidereals in principle.
notes: Chapter Four: Traits, 'Spells' -> 'Terrestrial Circle Sorcery' -> 'Open the Spirit Door', printed pp. 122-123 (PDF 125-126).

name: Gift of Knowledge
summary: Celestial Circle spell that lets the sorcerer directly transfer knowledge of a particular subject or skill -- an Ability, specialty, spell or Charm -- to another individual through an hour-long ritual of physical contact and deep meditative trance.
requirements: Prerequisite Charm: Celestial Circle Sorcery.
mechanics: The spell requires an hour-long ritual; the caster and the subject of the spell must be in physical contact, and both enter a deep meditative trance while knowledge flows from the sorcerer to the individual. It can impart a particular memory or understanding of a particular Trait, including Abilities, specialties, spells or Charms. It does not work on Essence. The spell obviates the need for training time for the Sidereal to learn the subject or improve the Trait, so long as the caster's rating in that Trait is greater than the subject's. The subject must have sufficient experience to improve the Trait and can only improve a Trait by one dot per casting of this spell, as with normal experience integration; however, multiple castings can allow a subject to increase a Trait in hours rather than weeks or months. Gift of Knowledge does not grant subjects the ability to learn Traits they cannot otherwise acquire, so it cannot teach a mortal to use Exalted Charms, for example, or a spell to a character who cannot cast it.
compatibility: Any Sidereal Exalted who has learned Celestial Circle Sorcery.
notes: Chapter Four: Traits, 'Spells' -> 'Celestial Circle Sorcery' -> 'Gift of Knowledge', printed p. 123 (PDF 126).

name: Summoning the Heavenly Portal
summary: Celestial Circle spell, kept especially secret by the Gold Faction, that opens the Calibration Gate -- a temporary gateway between Creation and Yu-Shan -- letting a Sidereal reach Heaven from anywhere in Creation in under 10 minutes.
requirements: Prerequisite Charm: Celestial Circle Sorcery.
mechanics: As the personal servants and messengers of the Five Maidens, the Sidereal Exalted were given knowledge of how to summon the Calibration Gate. To cast this spell, the Exalt must meditate and pray for five minutes; at the end of this time, the caster's player rolls the character's Essence + Occult. On a failure, some other Celestial Exalted used this spell recently, and the gate was not available; however, if the caster rolls even a single success, the gateway appears within arm's reach. The gateway normally stays until the next dawn, and it may not be summoned by another Exalt for half an hour after the caster summoned it. Almost no Solar Exalted know that this spell exists, and even most members of the Gold Faction fear what might happen if the Solars could travel as easily as they do; however, all Sidereals know that it is only a matter of time before some Noon Caste Exalt learns this spell, but they guard it jealously and will only give it to other Lunars they consider truly worthy. Lunar Exalted of the No Moon Caste know this spell, but are not capable of learning Celestial Circle Sorcery; their nature is too antithetical to Heaven's for them to possess any ability to command it. This spell can only be used in Creation and can only be used to call the gateway to Yu-Shan. A Sidereal can use this spell to gain access to Yu-Shan in less than 10 minutes; once in Yu-Shan, the caster cannot move this gateway. Instead, an Exalt desiring to move rapidly from one portion of Creation to another must summon this gateway, enter Yu-Shan and then leave it via a different gateway near her destination.
compatibility: Any Sidereal Exalted who has learned Celestial Circle Sorcery; No Moon Caste Lunars know this spell without being able to cast it themselves (they lack Celestial Circle Sorcery), and the Gold Faction closely guards knowledge of it from other Solars and Lunars.
notes: Chapter Four: Traits, 'Spells' -> 'Celestial Circle Sorcery' -> 'Summoning the Heavenly Portal', printed pp. 123-124 (PDF 126-127).

name: Prayer of the Chosen (Specialized Prayer)
summary: A once-common but now largely lost prayer technique, practiced today mainly by elder Sidereals (and some elder Lunars and Immaculate monastic societies), by which a single Exalted spends five days personally crafting three infused candles and then performs an hours-long ritual to bribe a single god with a guaranteed block of Ambrosia in exchange for favor.
requirements: Total of two or more dots in Occult and Savant (all Sidereals with this combination automatically know this prayer).
mechanics: The preparations for the prayer are simple but tedious and difficult to schedule. The Sidereal must fast for five days (one day for each Maiden) while personally creating three candles: one from Quintessence, one from the fat of a deceased mortal, and one from any type of material infused with the Exalted's own Essence. Forging the candles requires normal Craft rolls or Charms, but the character must infuse the third (Essence) candle with 10 motes of Essence, which become committed until after the prayer is over. On the sixth day, the Exalt enters a windowless, furniture-free chamber and places the candles in front of him. As he lights the Quintessence candle, the Sidereal says in a loud voice: 'Heavenly Essence Eternal, Burning Honorably in His (or Her) Favor.' The second candle, made from the mortal's fat, symbolizes Creation and the god's domain, and is portrayed through a whisper: 'Creation Burns in His (or Her) Honor.' The third candle, infused with the Sidereal's own Essence, symbolizes that although the Chosen is superior to the god in many ways, he still prays in the god's honor; as the flames burn, the Exalt must recite his own name and the reason he prays for the god's honor. The ritual takes no longer than four hours to perform. Roll the character's Charisma + Performance (specializations on the roll add to dice pool as normal), difficulty 1. Each success on the roll beyond the first supplies the god with an amount of Quintessence proportional to the number of successes rolled; in general, an Exalt must roll twice as many successes as the god's Essence to impress a deity. If the praying Sidereal has a permanent Essence rating of 5 or more, the player may choose to make a Charisma + Essence roll, difficulty 5, on the roll (instead of Quintessence success providing Quintessence, this variant supplies Ambrosia), but the character loses 15 motes of Personal Essence (instead of the motes being regained normally). Characters cannot offer physical sacrifices to better their chances with this prayer, nor does the character's priestly status modify the difficulty (see Exalted core rulebook, pp. 335-336). All Sidereals with a total of two or more dots in Occult and Savant know this prayer automatically. Note that bribing a god is a crime, and while normal mortal prayers (per Exalted core rulebook, pp. 335-336) go unnoticed, especially efficacious prayers such as this one will most certainly be noticed and recorded during periodic audits; characters with powerful political enemies or who make a habit of offending censors may find themselves charged with a Severity offense for each such prayer, its degree depending on the Essence of the god bribed and how far the deity deviated from the norms of her office to answer it -- generally a Severity 1 crime if the god did not answer the prayer (failing to report a bribe is also a crime) or a Severity 2 offense if she did answer it (see Chapter One, p. 36, for more on audits and Severity ratings).
cost: Committing 10 motes of Essence to the third (Essence-infused) candle for the duration of the ritual, regained normally afterward unless the character opts for the Essence-roll/Ambrosia variant, in which case 15 motes of Personal Essence are lost instead of being regained.
compatibility: Any Sidereal Exalted with two or more combined dots of Occult and Savant; also practiced by some elder Lunars and Immaculate monastic societies.
notes: Chapter Four: Traits, 'Specialized Prayers' -> 'Prayer of the Chosen', printed pp. 123-124 (PDF 126-127). This is one of two Specialized Prayers documented in this section; see sidereal-specialized-prayer-essence-prayer for the other.

name: Catalog of Colleges: The House of Journeys (The Captain, The Gull, The Mast, The Messenger, The Ship's Wheel)
summary: The five constellations of the House of Journeys -- the same five domains as the Journeys Caste's Auspicious Abilities (Sail/Thrown/Endurance/Ride/Survival) -- each given an ascending/descending thematic gloss, a Trappings description (how a resplendent destiny of that college dresses and behaves), a Correlations list (thematic keywords a Sidereal can invoke to justify unusual effects), and two to three named Resplendent Effects with their own effect-point/Paradox costs.
requirements: Initiation in the relevant college (see sidereal-character-creation-overview's 7-dot Colleges point-buy) to invoke ascending/descending effects per sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; Resplendent Effects additionally require having assumed that college's resplendent destiny (see resplendent-destinies).
mechanics: THE CAPTAIN: the college of strength, determination and orderliness (ascending); obsessive authority, paranoia of power and navel-gazing worship of organization (descending). Sign of the ship's officer/professional soldier, the work-gang boss and the stern matriarch. Trappings: wears an emblem of rank and carries a token of authority (a scepter or wand of office); is fearless and shows no sign of fatigue; is not kind, but is always fair and concerned for the wellbeing of his followers. Correlations: military command, fatherhood, tyranny, crystals, bureaucracy, discipline. Resplendent Effects -- Ship-Commanding Attitude (1 effect point/week): radiates intimidating charisma; adds Essence to Presence rolls to command and control a crew, but only so long as the character rules absolutely. Choosing for Fangs (1 effect point/month): naturally chooses the best, fearsome subordinates -- men able to work hard convincing him to love it gravitate to command; the Captain has no complaints from any underling with Valor lower than the Sidereal's Charisma, but cannot intimidate a subordinate who wants to quit into staying. Iron Drill Exercise (1 effect point/week): through personal example teaches followers a task; each week of drill grants followers 1 dot in an Ability, capped at the Sidereal's own rating in that Trait; can train up to (College rating x 10) individuals at once, and no individual can ever learn more Ability points from a Sidereal than that Sidereal's Conviction. THE GULL: the college of travel for its own sake, pure wanderlust without regard for profit -- both metaphysical and physical, the constellation of self-examination and inner change. Ascending: the wisdom of the outside perspective, the freedom of the wind-blown wanderer. Descending: rootlessness, thoughtless irresponsibility, shallow self-examination. Sign of the stray dog, the hobo, the wandering monk and laborer; sign of fish and migratory birds. Trappings: carries a staff and wears a traveler's cape; is dirty and hungry but happy; is not displeased with his rough lot. Correlations: wandering, wind, fish and birds, irresponsibility, rakish charisma, the unexamined life. Resplendent Effects -- Honest Face Spirit (1 effect point/week): hiring transient labor is difficult since crews are full of drunks and shiftless criminals; this effect assures that when the time comes to evaluate the character's trustworthiness for a menial job or insignificant responsibility, she is found acceptable regardless of her actual intentions. Good Worker Spirit (1 effect point/month): the Sidereal may not work an honest day, but knows how to look like she does; while active she is never accused of slacking no matter how little work she does. Joyous Grasshopper Spirit (1 effect point/season, 3 effect points for the season of Water): grants the Bon Vivant Nature in addition to her own, and each day on waking she may lower the target number of Conviction rolls made to regain Willpower by 1. THE MAST: the college of raw physical exertion and pure muscular strength. Ascending: heroic exertion providing the main strength for a task. Descending: strength without thought, unwillingness to question orders, stolid inability to communicate. College of the soldier, ditchdigger, scribe and house servant; sign of the insect. Trappings: drably dressed and unspeaking; is strong and honest but ignorant. Correlations: stoicism, tools, insects, architecture, manual labor, silence, the male phallus. Resplendent Effects -- Strength of the Mast (3 effect points, 1 Paradox die): so long as she is the strongest person present, her Strength is equal to any task; multiply Strength + Athletics by 10 to determine how much she can lift; does not work if the Mast is alone. Structure of the Mast (1 effect point): may add three dice to a roll so long as she is only passively supporting the task rather than actively assisting or performing a specialist's job. Invisible at the Center (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die/week): can find a menial job within a few hours in any populated area that will keep her fed, clothed and sheltered but nothing more; so long as she remains a silent, unquestioning menial laborer she avoids all legal, bureaucratic and official scrutiny -- those delivering summonses are powerless without supernatural tracking, and those following her must beat her Stamina + Athletics roll (her Essence added as automatic successes); she must live in a state of virtual servitude with only seven free hours per week. THE MESSENGER: the abode of the professional servant, symbolized by the horse-courier who braves danger to deliver precious information. Ascending: good, professional, brave service. Descending: service turned to bad ends, thoughtless abuse of power (associated with the Immaculate Inconsiderate Horseman heresy) and, more generally, abdication of moral responsibility. College of the courier, valet, aide, diplomat and the young Terrestrial Exalt in her cousins' household; sign of non-migratory birds, raptors and owls, and of service to one's family. Trappings: has a mount and is on urgent business; is daring and armed; carries a package from which she cannot be separated. Correlations: duty, raptors, bravery, arrogance, journeys, communication, selflessness, news. Resplendent Effects -- Iron Heart, Iron Horse (1 effect point/month): while carrying a message, neither the Sidereal nor her familiar/mount will ever fail a Valor roll that would delay the message or lengthen the route. Blow Wind Blow Style (1 effect point/week): the Sidereal and her mount make all Fatigue checks without modification for heat, cold, precipitation or other weather, and wake well-rested regardless of poor sleeping conditions. Field Mouse Rider (1 effect point, 3 Paradox dice/day): may cause any familiar to bear and carry her no matter how unsuitable it is as a mount; the familiar suffers no real ill effect beyond possible small fatigue penalties for a few days. THE SHIP'S WHEEL: the college of perseverance in the face of hardship, as a steersman lashes himself to the wheel so a ship can ride out a storm. Ascending: the success of perseverance. Descending: quixotic obsession and clinging to doomed causes. College of the steersman, the furnace-stoker, and those living wretchedly in pursuit of their beloved. Trappings: sleepless and unwashed, wearing a long cape or jacket and wristlets or a belt of rope; has a determined demeanor and lets no one share the burden of his post. Correlations: underdogs, cult beliefs, obsessive love, martyrdom, burdensome debt, wild animals as a group. Resplendent Effects -- Stronger Than This Job (1 effect point): so long as she has a job to do, Fatigue penalties are treated as bonus dice rather than penalties (so long as they would not reduce her pool below 0); once the task is done she takes unsoakable bashing damage equal to the Fatigue penalties absorbed. Marshaling Infinite Strength (1 effect point): so long as she was able to perform a task when she began it, she can finish it regardless of fatigue, condition or injury penalties suffered afterward; characters violently killed stay dead, but bodies/ghosts of those who die of natural causes or bleed out tend to keep performing their task until relieved. Poetic Sacrifice Insurance (2 effect points, 1 Paradox die): the player may roll again for any Sail or Survival roll made to travel in inclement weather and add the two rolls' successes together (Charms/effects boosting either roll must boost both separately); excess successes must be spent traveling farther than intended, however implausible the distance, and the character cannot stop traveling until they are used up.
cost: Each Resplendent Effect lists its own effect-point cost (and any added Paradox dice) alongside the standard astrology Effect Roll costs in sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; ascending/descending effects are costed via sidereal-astrology-scope-duration-power instead.
compatibility: Available to any Sidereal initiated in the relevant college; the base 5-difficulty Prayer Roll discount applies only to a Sidereal invoking a college within her own patron Maiden's house.
notes: 'The House of Journeys' and its five colleges (The Captain, The Gull, The Mast, The Messenger, The Ship's Wheel), printed pp. 220-222/PDF 223-225, immediately after the Catalog of Colleges' overview. Each college's name matches one of the Journeys Caste's five Auspicious Ability Charm trees (Sail 'The Captain', Thrown 'The Gull', Endurance 'The Mast', Ride 'The Messenger', Survival 'The Ship's Wheel'), confirming the book's one-to-one mapping between a house's colleges and its Caste's Auspicious Abilities. Each college's ascending/descending thematic write-up and Resplendent Effects are transcribed in summary/paraphrase rather than verbatim (matching this inventory's treatment of other large procedural/prose blocks); the generic Blessing/Curse effect types a Sidereal chooses from when using a college's ascending/descending powers are cataloged separately in sidereal-astrology-blessings-and-curses and are not re-derived per college here, since the book itself does not state which of the eight generic types each specific college favors beyond its thematic gloss.

name: Catalog of Colleges: The House of Leisure (The Ewer, The Lovers, The Musician, The Peacock, The Pillar)
summary: The five constellations of the House of Leisure -- the book's actual name for the house governing the same five domains as the Serenity Caste's Auspicious Abilities (Dodge/Socialize/Performance/Craft/Linguistics) -- each given an ascending/descending thematic gloss, Trappings, Correlations, and two to three named Resplendent Effects.
requirements: Initiation in the relevant college (see sidereal-character-creation-overview's 7-dot Colleges point-buy) to invoke ascending/descending effects per sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; Resplendent Effects additionally require having assumed that college's resplendent destiny (see resplendent-destinies).
mechanics: THE EWER: the sign of partnerships based on affection, romantic pursuit, or love of some other dream. Ascending: enduring adoration, flirtation, seduction, coquettish banter. Descending: the devouring mistrust of thoughtless, obsessive or impossible love. Sign of the marriage-seeker, the idealist, the revolutionary and the good monk; sign of incestuous couplings and amphibians. Trappings: bears flowers and a work of poetry; is blissfully happy and in love with love; wears his finest clothing to see his beloved. Correlations: love, motherhood, righteousness, idealism, monastic duty, seduction, dreams and fantasy. Resplendent Effects -- Sweet Flirtation Smile (1 effect point): may add the character's Charisma to any Bureaucracy, Socialize or Presence roll. Snappy Banter Approach (1 effect point): if the character's Wits is equal to or higher than the target's, may allow either party to reroll a failed social roll so the target does not fall under the Sidereal's sway. Frenzied Courtship Dodge (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die/week): makes the character an easy target for the arrows of love, drawing him into an ongoing courtship or (in strict cultures) difficult marriage negotiations within a day of arriving anywhere populated; he will never actually marry while the effect is active, but the courtship never ceases to be all-consuming; so long as he lives only for his beloved he avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat his Wits + Athletics roll, Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week). THE LOVERS: the sign of physical lust, carnal indulgence and uneven relationships. Ascending: relationships symbolically or situationally uneven, like a sex act. Descending: sexual depravity and the rape or capture of the helpless or entrapped. Sign of the fixed-price prostitute, the slave, the debtor, the beggar, the pedophile and all individuals engaging in sex acts, as well as vermin/rodents and Fair Folk Ravagers and their victims. Trappings: dressed in silk robes with rumpled hair; superficially friendly and attractive but betraying some sign of violence or restraint, even if only love-bites. Correlations: service, submission, slaves, vermin, Ravagers, lust, the sex act, rape, abuse. Resplendent Effects -- Handsome Boy Eyes (1 effect point): can attempt a seduction roll on a target without looking at or speaking to them, merely seeing them from across a room. Celestial Bliss Trick (1 effect point/performance): a simple trick that brings total sexual ecstasy within three minutes; the target's player must succeed at a Willpower and Temperance roll (difficulty 1) or fall under the Sidereal's sway. Whore-and-Virgin Stance (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die/week): the character becomes a worshiped god or a possessed object (per her tastes), becoming a kept courtesan or pimped prostitute within a day of arriving anywhere populated; so long as she lives an empty life of sex and submission she avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat her Manipulation + Presence roll, Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week). THE MUSICIAN: the sign of joy-in-plenty and enjoyment of the finer things -- college of gourmets, gluttons and poets. Descending: hollow avarice, blind materialism and scandalous excess; under Sidereal influence this constellation is called the Painted Boy in Immaculate practice, since it is also the sign of homosexual couplings that travel in small family groups. Trappings: wears facial makeup, dresses outlandishly and always carries a musical instrument; is cynically wise and uninhibited. Correlations: excess, laughter, hedonism, music, homosexuality, drug use, finery, greed, extramarital pairings, contentment in living, theater. Resplendent Effects -- Strange Days (1 effect point): may force anyone presented with a possible source of gratification or intoxication to make a Temperance roll or succumb, even if the target would never normally consider it. Impossible-to-Remember Party Approach (1 effect point/night): while performing (holding court, conversing, or performing music/dance), the difficulty for everyone nearby's Temperance rolls increases by 1. Brigand-and-Carouser Attracting Style (1 effect point/week, 1 Paradox die): by going home with a barmaid or attending a teahouse/tavern party, attaches himself to a family or friendship group of marginal personalities (brigands, louts, or rejects) who accept him as one of their own by day's end; so long as he lives large with this troupe he avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat his Stamina + Presence roll, Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week). THE PEACOCK: the sign of practical alliance, thoughtful breeding and considered partnerships -- as the peahen chooses a cock by his tail, those under this sign weigh a prospective mate's advantages carefully. Descending: loveless marriages, forced alliances, half-functional partnerships. Sign of the courtesan, the goodwife, the thoughtful matriarch, the established Dragon-Blooded household, and predators who hunt in packs. Trappings: struts magnificent finery (gang stylings, armor, or court clothing); is proud, has excellent taste, and is obviously sexually available. Correlations: greed, love for wealth's sake, procreation, dualities, alliances, bright colors, necessity, traps, distraction. Resplendent Effects -- Proper Plumage (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die): given access to a large closet, second-hand clothing store, or pile of cloth scraps, can always look good enough to gain +1 to Appearance-based rolls at any social event regardless of setting or attire norms. Spouse-Saving Grace (1 effect point): whenever present with his/her mate and the mate's player fails a Bureaucracy or Socialize roll, may spend a point of Conviction or Temperance to have his/her own player make the roll instead. Wife-Procuring Tailfeathers (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die/week): an obvious catch and an expert judge of catches, finds himself married and managing a large, prosperous household within a week of arriving anywhere populated; so long as he lives as full-time family manager he avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat his Charisma + Bureaucracy roll, Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week). THE PILLAR: the sign of partnerships tested and found stable -- the just empress, the just matriarch, the caring parent. Descending: bad parenting, and partnerships/authority tested and found wanting. Sign of the asexual partner (mother, business partner, drinking buddy), of service in the Thousand Scales, and of herd animals such as mammoth and elk. Trappings: wears a wedding ring and dresses plainly; is perceptive and practical; is firm but just. Correlations: family, friendship, stability, civil society, unjust authority, stagnation, queens and princes. Resplendent Effects -- Comforting Matriarch Embrace (1 effect point): may hold and comfort another person before putting him to sleep; on waking, his player may roll the character's Conviction twice to regain Willpower. Equitable Partnership (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die): can find a monetary backer for a business plan well-funded to match the plan's plausible merit; cannot use this to swindle anyone, but a good idea need never sit idle for lack of funds. Best Friend's Couch (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die/week): by approaching the nearest habitation where the character speaks the language, presents herself as a long-lost friend and is fed and housed (floor, couch, or spare bed) as well as anyone in the house; cannot stay anywhere long and must move to a new house every few days as the welcome wears out, but so long as she spends her time with these newfound friends she avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat her Charisma + Presence roll, Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week).
cost: Each Resplendent Effect lists its own effect-point cost (and any added Paradox dice) alongside the standard astrology Effect Roll costs in sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; ascending/descending effects are costed via sidereal-astrology-scope-duration-power instead.
compatibility: Available to any Sidereal initiated in the relevant college; the base 5-difficulty Prayer Roll discount applies only to a Sidereal invoking a college within her own patron Maiden's house.
notes: 'The House of Leisure' and its five colleges (The Ewer, The Lovers, The Musician, The Peacock, The Pillar), printed pp. 223-225/PDF 226-228, immediately after the House of Journeys. The book names this house 'The House of Leisure,' not 'The House of Serenity' as the earlier sidereal-astrology-procedure-and-catalog-overview row's notes anticipated -- corrected here to match the actual printed heading. Each college's name matches one of the Serenity Caste's five Auspicious Ability Charm trees (Dodge 'The Ewer', Socialize 'The Lovers', Performance 'The Musician', Craft 'The Peacock', Linguistics 'The Pillar'), continuing the book's one-to-one mapping between a house's colleges and its Caste's Auspicious Abilities. The Musician's Strange Days Resplendent Effect description spans the pp. 223-224/PDF 226-227 page break and the Pillar's Best Friend's Couch spans pp. 224-225/PDF 227-228; both were reassembled as single continuous effects. Ascending/descending write-ups and Resplendent Effects are transcribed in summary/paraphrase rather than verbatim, matching the House of Journeys row's treatment.

name: Catalog of Colleges: The House of War (The Banner, The Gauntlet, The Quiver, The Shield, The Spear)
summary: The five constellations of the House of War -- the book's name for the house governing the same five domains as the Battles Caste's Auspicious Abilities (Presence/Brawl/Archery/Resistance/Melee) -- each given an ascending/descending thematic gloss, Trappings, Correlations, and two to three named Resplendent Effects.
requirements: Initiation in the relevant college (see sidereal-character-creation-overview's 7-dot Colleges point-buy) to invoke ascending/descending effects per sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; Resplendent Effects additionally require having assumed that college's resplendent destiny (see resplendent-destinies).
mechanics: THE BANNER: the sign of reputation, story and awe. Ascending: governs fame, glory, heroic reputation and leadership. Descending: the use of terror as a weapon, wild-eyed panic of rumor, infamy, uninspiring leadership and living on reputation. Sign of the rumormonger, the crier, the witness, the martyr, the tyrant and all those possessing heroic renown. Trappings: strikingly clad and always among you; is fearless, victorious and larger than life. Correlations: reputation, pageantry, leadership, epics, infamy, reigns of terror, philanthropy, tidings, symbols, heraldry. Resplendent Effects -- Heroic General Presence (2 effect points/scene): exhibits himself at the forefront of battle; the difficulty of all Valor checks for those under his direct command is reduced to 1. Battle-Fellow Attitude (1 effect point/month): can draw back any soldier who has ever fought for him by publicly posting that he is calling up troops; thereafter, each week the effect is in place, every soldier who ever served under his direct command must make a difficulty-2 Willpower roll or come to serve beneath his banner again. Tide of History (3 effect points, 1 Paradox die/month): troops marching beneath his banner fight without fear or hesitation as if their cause were endorsed by history itself, never failing difficulty-1 Valor checks or suffering wound/fatigue penalties (they can be worked or marched to death but will not complain or slacken). THE GAUNTLET: the college of the choice between bad and worse, of ruthless expediency and battlefield logic. Ascending: the courage to undertake unpleasant necessities. Descending: callousness, ruthlessness, and a willingness to justify the whims of the moment as necessity. Home to the sergeant, the martinet, the surgeon, the judge, the policeman, the thug in uniform and the practical matriarch. Trappings: bloodstained and brutal; wears a uniform and carries a cudgel; makes meaningless demands and then punishes those who do not obey. Correlations: sergeants, confrontation, callousness, sacrifice of others, necessity, livestock management, pragmatism, surgery, the greater good. Resplendent Effects -- Weak-Spine Sense (1 effect point/week): instantly knows who among people facing her is intimidated by or frightened of her, and to what degree. Knuckle-Cracking Stance (1 effect point): may add her Essence to an intimidation attempt, but the target perceives her as using physical Attributes as part of the roll. Thug Fist (2 effect points, 1 Paradox die): activated reflexively before an attack roll; if her next unarmed attack does damage, the target permanently loses 1 Appearance to disfigurement. THE QUIVER: the college of flexibility and fleetness of thought -- as an archer has many arrows in her quiver, a character under this sign has many ideas and stratagems. Ascending: quick-wittedness and versatility. Descending: stupidity explained convincingly and thinking in lockstep with one's peers ('just another arrow in the quiver'). Sign of the duelist, the know-it-all, the Dragon-Blooded in secondary school, the socialite, the general, the quick-witted scholar and the urbane boor. Trappings: carries a bow or a map case; is clever and witty; his valor matters less than his education. Correlations: strategy, choices, haste, pride, archery, boorishness, self-absorption. Resplendent Effects -- Apologetic Feint (1 effect point): can rephrase a demand to make it look like an acceptable compromise; on any roll involving a Social Attribute, may reflexively roll a number of dice equal to that Attribute and add the successes to the roll's total, even after dice are already counted. Instant Genius Style (1 effect point): may make any Intelligence + Lore, Intelligence + Occult, or Intelligence + Bureaucracy roll that would normally require long research time immediately -- the character simply knows the answer. Several Arrows of Reason (1 effect point per three arrows, 1 Paradox die): arms the character with several arrows of reason that ignore gossamer armor and cause any creature outside fate they strike and damage to become part of fate until the end of the scene; the arrows themselves dissipate at scene's end. THE SHIELD: the house of the ecstatic warrior who seeks battle without regard for victory -- also the college of those who fight and die for their peers or draw strength from pain. Ascending: courage and heroism without regard for consequences. Descending: sadism, masochism, suicidal bravery and battle literally without thought. Sign of scouts, assassins, heroic warriors and lone predators who hunt with teeth and claw. Trappings: always carries a shield and a leather strap for biting; is always armed and eager for battle; carries trophies of his kills. Correlations: barbarians and the barbarian code, fearlessness, protection, bragging, pain, heroism, heroic suicide, wrath, Lunars. Resplendent Effects -- Wounded Lion Strength (2 effect points): may add dice to a single attack's damage equal to the number of health levels of damage she's currently suffering, added before armor is applied. Hero's Iron Skin (3 effect points/scene): so long as wearing no armor, has the effect of +9L/+9B armor, treated as natural soak for effects that penetrate armor. Aspect of the Bear (2 effect points, 1 Paradox die/scene): transforms the character's anima banner into the shape of a great bear; anyone who sees the banner must make a difficulty-1 Valor roll to face the Sidereal, and while in this state the Sidereal cannot fail Valor rolls or suffer Valor penalties. THE SPEAR: the sign of skill and discipline in armed conflict. Ascending: skill, professionalism and discipline. Descending: superficial professionalism, professional myopia, and inability to see solutions outside one's own scope of interest. Sign of the bodyguard, the long-service professional soldier, the skilled militiaman, the arms instructor, the mercenary, and other skilled professional competitors such as the gambler, the gladiator and the athlete. Trappings: wears a uniform but possesses no rank; is called by family name or nickname; is disciplined and brave. Correlations: soldiers, bodyguards, bravery, professionalism, training, taking initiative, lack of vision, tactics, skillfulness, competition. Resplendent Effects -- Someone's Son Style (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die/lunar month): common folk of all cultures know an honest soldier stays out of politics; so long as the Exalt makes no pretensions, protects them with his weapons, and avoids drawing war to them, they will aid and feed him even without sharing a language, asking no questions and never revealing his location to enemy troops; so long as he maintains this compact and keeps his weapon close, he avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat his Stamina + Presence roll, Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week). Hero-Supporting Performance (1 effect point/scene): if anyone in the Sidereal's unit can do something, so can he -- for the rest of the scene he may accept the highest Athletics success total anyone in the unit has rolled, and can likewise carry his share using the Strength + Athletics total of the strongest person helping him lift. Battle-Carrying Presence (1 effect point/scene): no one fighting under the Sidereal's direct command can fail a Valor check unless they (or the Sidereal) suffer a wound or Fatigue penalty higher than his own.
cost: Each Resplendent Effect lists its own effect-point cost (and any added Paradox dice) alongside the standard astrology Effect Roll costs in sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; ascending/descending effects are costed via sidereal-astrology-scope-duration-power instead.
compatibility: Available to any Sidereal initiated in the relevant college; the base 5-difficulty Prayer Roll discount applies only to a Sidereal invoking a college within her own patron Maiden's house.
notes: 'The House of War' and its five colleges (The Banner, The Gauntlet, The Quiver, The Shield, The Spear), printed pp. 226-228/PDF 229-231, immediately after the House of Leisure. Each college's name matches one of the Battles Caste's five Auspicious Ability Charm trees (Presence 'The Banner', Brawl 'The Gauntlet', Archery 'The Quiver', Resistance 'The Shield', Melee 'The Spear'), continuing the book's one-to-one mapping between a house's colleges and its Caste's Auspicious Abilities. Ascending/descending write-ups and Resplendent Effects are transcribed in summary/paraphrase rather than verbatim, matching the prior two house rows' treatment.

name: Catalog of Colleges: The House of Secrets (The Guardians, The Key, The Mask, The Sorcerer, The Treasure Trove)
summary: The five constellations of the House of Secrets -- the book's name for the house governing the same five domains as the Secrets Caste's Auspicious Abilities (Larceny/Investigation/Stealth/Occult/Lore) -- each given an ascending/descending thematic gloss, Trappings, Correlations, and two to three named Resplendent Effects; the Mask is also the college specifically damaged by the Sidereal Exalted's own post-Purge concealment, which is why Sidereals cannot use its ascending/descending effects on themselves.
requirements: Initiation in the relevant college (see sidereal-character-creation-overview's 7-dot Colleges point-buy) to invoke ascending/descending effects per sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; Resplendent Effects additionally require having assumed that college's resplendent destiny (see resplendent-destinies); the Mask's ascending/descending effects cannot be self-targeted by a Sidereal (only its Resplendent Effects can), per arcane-fate.
mechanics: THE GUARDIANS: the college of practical knowledge and rewards earned through long labor, containing the wisdom of the beast and the elderly. Ascending: a fundamental understanding of the nature of Creation from long observation or inbred wisdom. Descending: quackery and meaningless superstition. Sign of the shaman, the snake-oil salesman, the talisman seller, the midwife and the old duffer. Trappings: uneducated and carries a talisman; is suspicious, knows the weather, and has a wisdom that can aid you in your current task. Correlations: hearth wisdom, respect for the elderly, age, superstition, charlatans and mountebanks, tradition, patience, observation, inevitability. Resplendent Effects -- Lazy Works Smart Style (1 effect point): -2 to the difficulty of any Athletics roll for physical labor, but only if the extra successes are used to shorten the time the task takes. Hayseed Eye (1 effect point/week): can detect if someone interacting with her has hostile intentions -- not a preternatural danger sense, but the ability to tell whether someone is planning to take advantage of the Sidereal. Talisman-Making Touch (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die): creates a talisman of any type from a personal possession or object she blesses (the Sidereal and circumstance determine the talisman's exact nature); it cannot be kept and must be given to one in need. THE KEY: the college of wisdom discovered through scholarly study and intellectual understanding, and generally the astrological sign of rewards gained and tasks accomplished by cleverness. Ascending: experimentation, inquiry, sharp thinking and new solutions. Descending: pointless or wasteful experiments, tinkering with things best left undisturbed, and sharp practice. Sign of the tinker and the junk seller, and of monkeys and other primates. Trappings: carries a measuring stick and a pen, but no wax tablet or notebook; claims innocence but has a dishonest expression; is a creature of large appetites. Correlations: innovation, hubris, corruption, automata and mechanical devices, books, libraries, medicine, curiosity. Resplendent Effects -- Never Cease Moving (1 effect point/week): so long as making preparations for a Lore or Bureaucracy roll, he need only sleep an hour a day and can live on Essence alone. Ascending Destiny Mien (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die/week): may lower the difficulty by 1 when interacting with anyone whose Temperance is lower than the Exalt's Intelligence. Provable Location of the Gate (1 effect point, 3 Paradox dice): proves through measurements and mathematical formulas that the Calibration Gate is present right at his current location, and so it is (may be a slight delay if the gate is actually elsewhere). THE MASK: the college of secret wisdom, of things known but concealed. Ascending: religious mystery, rites of passage and the secrets of the bed. Descending: humbug, deliberate obfuscation and the mountebank. Sign of the spy, the priest and the librarian. This sign was damaged by the Sidereal Exalted shortly after the Solar Purge, when the Chosen of the Maidens twisted their own destiny again and again to conceal their existence; as a result, Sidereals suffer the Arcane Fate (see arcane-fate) and cannot use this college's ascending or descending effects on themselves, only its Resplendent Effects. Trappings: wears a mask over his face and clothes of soft fabric; is quiet and does not announce himself; clings to sacred places and lingers around Manses and Demesnes. Correlations: secrets, lies, security services, guarded individuals, religious worship, extortion, trickery. Resplendent Effects -- Privacy-Enhancing Gesture (1 effect point): the area within (Essence x 10) yards of the character becomes proof against supernatural scrying, teleportation and other forms of intrusion, including Everywhere and Nowhere Technique. Foot Treads No Twig (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die): may reroll a single Dexterity + Stealth roll before it is compared to an enemy's roll. Everywhere and Nowhere Technique (1 effect point, 3 Paradox dice/week): can conceal herself in the most unlikely places -- between raindrops, between moments, behind curtains on a dusty stair in a faraway town -- eating from food others overlook and sleeping only in secret places no eye can linger on; nobody sees the character, but she sees much; so long as she persists in this furtive occult existence she avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat her Intelligence + Occult roll, her College + Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week to spy on anyone within a number of miles equal to her Essence, so long as those places are not themselves proof against scrying/intrusion). THE SORCERER: some secrets are worth more than others, and those of the College of the Sorcerer are the valuable sort -- the secrets of power. Sign of the Exalt, the god, the geomancer and the talisman maker. Ascending: artifice, sorcery and geomancy. Descending: the black arts of demon summoning and necromancy. Astrological sign of tasks accomplished through the use of Essence. Sidereal Exalted commonly use this college to set up front identities as (visibly) Exalted so they can conduct business in Heaven and with other Exalted; most Sidereals don't keep such an identity for more than 100 years. Trappings: is one of the Exalted and a prince of the earth, displaying goods of the Five Magical Materials, a Caste Mark, and a regal bearing; wears armor and carries a daiklave. Correlations: humanity, geomancy, artifice, demon summoning and infernalism, talismans, Essence use, egotism, Yozi-slaves. Resplendent Effects -- Invincible Essence Core (1 effect point): if targeted by a hostile effect that would lower permanent Essence, cause memory loss, or cause loss of access to spells/Charms/Combos/Abilities, may reflexively spend 1 effect point to block that effect. Prince of the Earth (1 effect point/scene): may have many peers but no superiors; +3 to all social rolls with the unExalted so long as acting the part of an Exalt (without implying a sense of superiority). Seer (X effect points): when taking part in astrology to determine or plan the future alongside another Sidereal, may spend any number of effect points to give that Sidereal's attempt bonus dice; mutual endorsement of resplendent Exaltation petitions and staged lengthy rituals for maximum effect is a hallmark of major Sidereal gatherings. THE TREASURE TROVE: the college of revealed wisdom, of understanding and knowledge held up like a beacon for the world, and generally the sign of rewards earned and tasks accomplished by excellence. Ascending: erudition, education and enlightenment. Descending: intellectual elitism, pointless cerebration, the bookworm and the know-it-all. College of the teacher, the revolutionary, the prophet, and the savant, as well as of animals that hunt by stinging or leaping upon their prey. Trappings: carries a book of wisdom and wears scholar's robes; is poor in money but educated in formal learning; is deeply impractical but well-meaning. Correlations: horoscopes, schools, scholarship, savants, blight, blindness, inflexibility, secret societies, prophecies. Resplendent Effects -- Stab the Seer's Eye (1 effect point/season): instantly aware of any mortal astrological inquiry about her, and can cause it to produce any reading she pleases. Dismissive Scholar's Sniff (1 effect point): may always appeal to an authority yet unread, adding her Essence to any Lore or Bureaucracy roll made in argument with someone whose Lore or Bureaucracy is lower than or equal to her own. Professorial Mien (1 effect point/month): those around the character treat her as cultured and educated, turning to her to resolve linguistic disputes and solve difficult problems; may add her Essence to Presence or Socialize rolls, but only when her Lore is higher than the target's Intelligence.
cost: Each Resplendent Effect lists its own effect-point cost (and any added Paradox dice) alongside the standard astrology Effect Roll costs in sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; ascending/descending effects are costed via sidereal-astrology-scope-duration-power instead.
compatibility: Available to any Sidereal initiated in the relevant college; the base 5-difficulty Prayer Roll discount applies only to a Sidereal invoking a college within her own patron Maiden's house; the Mask's ascending/descending effects can never be self-targeted regardless of house.
notes: 'The House of Secrets' and its five colleges (The Guardians, The Key, The Mask, The Sorcerer, The Treasure Trove), printed pp. 228-230/PDF 231-233, immediately after the House of War. Each college's name matches one of the Secrets Caste's five Auspicious Ability Charm trees (Larceny 'The Guardians', Investigation 'The Key', Stealth 'The Mask', Occult 'The Sorcerer', Lore 'The Treasure Trove'), continuing the book's one-to-one mapping between a house's colleges and its Caste's Auspicious Abilities. The Mask's write-up explicitly cross-references and elaborates on the Arcane Fate mechanic (arcane-fate) as the in-fiction reason Sidereals cannot use this specific college's ascending/descending effects on themselves. Ascending/descending write-ups and Resplendent Effects are transcribed in summary/paraphrase rather than verbatim, matching the prior three house rows' treatment.

name: Catalog of Colleges: The House of Endings (The Corpse, The Crow, The Haywain, The Rising Smoke, The Sword)
summary: The five constellations of the House of Endings -- the book's name for the house governing the same five domains as the Endings Caste's Auspicious Abilities (Medicine/Awareness/Bureaucracy/Athletics/Martial Arts) -- each given an ascending/descending thematic gloss, Trappings, Correlations, and two to three named Resplendent Effects; this is the last of the five houses, closing out the Catalog of Colleges' 25 constellations.
requirements: Initiation in the relevant college (see sidereal-character-creation-overview's 7-dot Colleges point-buy) to invoke ascending/descending effects per sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; Resplendent Effects additionally require having assumed that college's resplendent destiny (see resplendent-destinies).
mechanics: THE CORPSE: the college of the end of lives, both literally and (in the metaphorical sense) of modes of existence. Ascending: existences end with planning, dignity and grace. Descending: existences end with agony and wailing. Constellation of the affianced youth, the family moving house, the middle-aged man forced to change professions, and the sign of the dragonfly and other non-amphibious creatures that metamorphose halfway through their lives. Trappings: wears his best clothes; is calm and bears the emblem of a butterfly somewhere on his person; carries a textbook that may be a guide to a new trade or to the Underworld; like the Sword, is unshod. Correlations: quick and painless deaths, exits, sudden change, transformation, unfinished business, shapechangers, thresholds. Resplendent Effects -- Dignity of the Dead (1 effect point): may ignore the effect of one lost Social roll with no ill effects. Shadow of the Reaper (3 effect points, 1 Paradox die): by making the Superior Sign of the Corpse, fills the target with intimations of mortality, causing the target to lose all temporary Willpower in excess of her permanent Conviction. Rising Butterfly Prayer (3 effect points, 3 Paradox dice): by reciting a short homily and burning a silk memorial to Lytek (with a copy to Taru-Han) at a formal funeral or grave immediately after, can request that an individual's soul receive due (though not guaranteed) consideration by the Division of Abstract Matters for reincarnation into a body chosen for Terrestrial Exaltation; any delay beyond the funeral risks the request arriving too late for processing. THE CROW: the college of the end of illusions and dreams, and of inevitability and its recognition. Ascending: comfort in death, morbid humor, and the heroism of the forlorn hope. Descending: a rush to death disguised as acceptance, the false bravado behind the skull mask of the Calibration dancers, and indifference to others' suffering. College of the ancestors and the ancestor cult, of the young widow and the old man, and the sign of death by old age. Trappings: carries black feathers and wears a black cloak; is morbidly humorous and clever, and attracted to shiny objects. Correlations: slow and painless deaths, inevitability, ancestors, widows and orphans, acceptance of death, dark humor, waking, indifference. Resplendent Effects -- Reading Dead Eyes (1 effect point): by eating a corpse's eye, learns the last thing the corpse saw before dying, seeing the target's final scene and becoming aware if the target is a ghost or hungry ghost. Bold Filcher (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die): can take something from plain sight; witnesses must win an opposed Perception + Awareness roll against the character's Dexterity + Larceny to notice. Feathered Cloak Trick (3 effect points, 3 Paradox dice/day): makes the Superior Sign of the Crow and turns into a raven, crow or other corvid with Strength and Stamina of 1, the character's own Dexterity, health levels, Social/Mental Attributes and Abilities, a 0L/1B soak, with all equipment transforming along with her. THE HAYWAIN: the college of endings that cannot be easily described -- the gradual decline and failure of systems with fuzzy boundaries and imprecise definitions: the broken circle, the faltering alliance, the deteriorating government, the troubled family. Ascending: ruin gives way to new growth. Descending: leads to placid stasis and bucolic decay. College of death by sorcery, divinity, and senescent senility; sign of the Dragon-Blooded retiree. Trappings: wears dishevelled robes and an informal attitude; is hard of hearing but demands bribes; is arrogant, ambitious and unconcerned with the big picture. Correlations: muddled deaths, mystery, cover-ups, treachery, comebacks, aging and decrepitude. Resplendent Effects -- Harvest Ripe Wheat, Father Falling Hay (1 effect point): by waiting in a reception area or visiting a shop floor, learns whether a business or bureau is 'wholly corrupt,' 'mostly corrupt,' 'somewhat corrupt,' 'mostly honest,' or 'totally honest' as an organizational whole (not about specific individuals); can alternatively be used on a contemplated misdeed to learn whether it 'will not,' 'may possibly,' or 'is certain to' receive official scrutiny at the moment the opportunity to commit it arises. Old Fellows Society Luncheon (1 effect point): by approaching any meeting of officials or merchants in a populated business/bureaucratic community, immediately ingratiates himself and gains a position of great importance but little responsibility in a government bureau or business by day's end, filling his existence with meetings, junkets and dinners thereafter; so long as he immerses himself in this purposeless upward mobility he avoids all legal/bureaucratic/official scrutiny (pursuers must beat his Wits + Bureaucracy roll, Essence as automatic successes; only seven free hours per week). Celestial Intervention Appeal (1 effect point, 5 Paradox dice): makes the Superior Sign of the Haywain and summons the most severe available heavenly censor (of the Bureau of Heaven, not Destiny) to attend to a legal or security matter of Celestial import, typically arriving via the Portal Charm, possibly with a retinue of celestial lions/thunderbirds/huraka; this is a serious, politically sensitive call for outside attention that implicitly admits the Bureau of Destiny cannot handle the situation itself. THE RISING SMOKE: the college of the end of journeys, both literally and for metaphorical paths like initiation, puberty and apprenticeship. College of the young man, the journeyman, the corpse en route to burial, the not-yet-Exalted pubescent Dynast, and those facing charges or lawsuits. Ascending: paths end in transformation to a new state. Descending: bootless errands and death by accident, heart attack, stroke or murder. Trappings: carries good-luck prayer strips, a purse of money from her teacher, and brand-new journeyman's equipment; is optimistic and naive. Correlations: quick and painful deaths, rest, stagnation, growth, chance, new employment, fresh prospects, murder. Resplendent Effects -- Record-Obtaining Inquiry (1 effect point): may add her Essence to any roll involving Charisma made with a god, judge, or magistrate. Superior-Entreating Memorial Style (1 effect point): burns a letter of fine silk addressed to a fellow Sidereal, which appears discreetly hidden against the recipient's skin (requiring a 6+ success Perception + Awareness roll to notice its arrival); the recipient may annotate and return it free of charge within three days for the same subtle delivery back to the sender. Chains of Adorjan (3 effect points, 1 or 3 Paradox dice): makes the Superior Sign of the Rising Smoke and summons the deadly, silent wind of the Demon Realm to scour a touched target for 13 turns, dealing damage as if from a demon; each turn the target's player must make a reflexive difficulty-4 Stamina + Resistance roll, taking 1A on a success or 4A on a failure (in Creation, Adorjan's winds are attenuated, so this damage applies automatically rather than reflexively). THE SWORD: the college of the end of hope. Ascending: not the constellation of fulfillment itself, but of the individual continuing on without that hope's assistance once it is realized. Descending: hopes and dreams wither and die; also the constellation of the broken, the crushed and the worn down. College of the salesman, the has-been, the virgin, the ghost and the pregnant woman; sign of death after prolonged suffering and illness. Trappings: is worn out; carries or wears a withered flower and dresses in burial cerements; weeps but cannot be consoled; is unshod. Correlations: slow and painful deaths, perseverance, failure, illness, tribulation, inheritance, resignation, the vanquished. Resplendent Effects -- Style-Discerning Eye (1 effect point, 1 Paradox die): reflexively activated whenever the Exalt clearly observes another individual activate a Martial Arts Charm the Sidereal doesn't know, letting her learn that Charm's trick without a tutor (still requires normal doubled training time, spent experience, and meeting prerequisites/Minimum Ability/Essence); the stolen knowledge fades after a year and a day. Minimum Legal Defense Competence (1 effect point): may make a parry or dodge attempt at full dice pool against an attack, but that defense cannot be enhanced by Charms, Virtues, Willpower, or any other effect. Tears of the Blade (3 effect points, 1 Paradox die): those who see the apparition of the College of the Sword are doomed; making the Superior Sign of the Sword at one individual causes mortals to be slain instantly or die horribly within five days (Exalt's choice), and causes any Exalted subject to the gesture to die instantly and irrevocably the next time they are reduced to Incapacitated or below (lasting the rest of a Terrestrial Exalt's life, but only a year and a day for a Celestial Exalt); has no effect on beings outside of fate or on gods and elementals.
cost: Each Resplendent Effect lists its own effect-point cost (and any added Paradox dice) alongside the standard astrology Effect Roll costs in sidereal-astrology-effect-roll; ascending/descending effects are costed via sidereal-astrology-scope-duration-power instead.
compatibility: Available to any Sidereal initiated in the relevant college; the base 5-difficulty Prayer Roll discount applies only to a Sidereal invoking a college within her own patron Maiden's house.
notes: 'The House of Endings' and its five colleges (The Corpse, The Crow, The Haywain, The Rising Smoke, The Sword), printed pp. 231-235/PDF 234-238, immediately after the House of Secrets; this is the fifth and final house, closing out all 25 constellations of the Catalog of Colleges. Each college's name matches one of the Endings Caste's five Auspicious Ability Charm trees (Medicine 'The Corpse', Awareness 'The Crow', Bureaucracy 'The Haywain', Athletics 'The Rising Smoke', Martial Arts 'The Sword'), completing the book's one-to-one mapping between each house's colleges and its Caste's Auspicious Abilities across all five houses. Chains of Adorjan's exact Paradox-die/duration wording (whether the 1-die or 3-die case applies to a demon vs. non-demon target) reads ambiguously/inconsistently in the source and was paraphrased as faithfully as possible rather than resolved by guesswork; flagged here for a closer re-read before any promotion. Superior-Entreating Memorial Style's description spans the pp. 234-235/PDF 237-238 page break and was reassembled as one continuous effect. Ascending/descending write-ups and Resplendent Effects are transcribed in summary/paraphrase rather than verbatim, matching the prior four house rows' treatment. Immediately after this house, the book opens a new 'Greater Signs' section (printed p. 235/PDF 238) describing a distinct, more powerful astrology mechanic tied to the Five Maidens' own gestures rather than to individual colleges; that section is out of scope for this row and is inventoried separately.

name: Sidereal Astrology Greater Signs
summary: Greater Signs are the Sidereal astrology equivalent of an ultimate technique -- the Five Maidens' own reality-shaping gestures, once used to order the universe before the pattern spiders existed, which a sufficiently advanced Chosen of a Maiden can reflexively mimic to produce a house-wide area effect (instant mass travel, dispelling all magic, capping incoming damage, revealing beings outside fate, or converting damage into automatic successes) at the cost of permanent Essence and Willpower.
requirements: Permanent Essence 4 or higher; must be a Chosen of the Maiden whose Greater Sign is being mimicked; must have a minimum rating of 3 in all five colleges of that Maiden's astrological house (i.e., all five colleges of the matching House row).
mechanics: Greater Signs are to Sidereal astrology what prayer strips are to Sidereal Charms: they culminate in power far surpassing an ordinary astrology effect. These are the Five Maidens' own gestures, once used to order the universe in the time before the pattern spiders existed; their effect is lessened by being mimicked by the Maidens' Chosen rather than performed by a Maiden herself, but they completely bypass the pattern spiders and operate directly on the fabric of the Tapestry, retaining immense power. Making a Greater Sign is a reflexive action costing 10 motes, 1 permanent Essence and 1 permanent Willpower; the effect supersedes (cannot be combined with) the Lesser Sign of that Maiden's house, i.e., the Sidereal's own anima banner. The Greater Sign of Mercury (Sign of Travel): manifests as a brilliant yellow aura (16+ anima-banner-level) around the Exalt; lets her instantly move herself and a number of allies up to her Essence to any location that is part of fate (excluding the Jade Pleasure Dome and the Lotus of Destiny); she must travel with them to guide them. The Greater Sign of Venus (Sign of Serenity): brilliant blue aura; instantly and silently snuffs out all Essence effects within a radius of miles equal to the Exalt's Essence that are not Solar Circle Sorcery or the doing of a Celestial Incarna, including non-permanent Charm enhancements, Terrestrial/Celestial Circle Sorcery, Sidereal astrology, artifact powers, and other magical effects. The Greater Sign of Mars (Sign of War): brilliant ruby aura; for a number of hours equal to the Exalt's Essence, all attacks by allies against foes caught within a radius of miles equal to her Essence deal a maximum raw pre-soak damage equal to the attacker's own Essence (armor still reduces this normally); beings entering the aura are bound by the effect for its full duration even if they later leave. The Greater Sign of Jupiter (Sign of Secrets): brilliant green aura; for a number of hours equal to the Exalt's Essence, all beings outside of fate caught within a radius of miles equal to her Essence are temporarily made part of the Tapestry as if successfully affected by a Charm; same enter/leave duration-lock rule as Mars. The Greater Sign of Saturn (Sign of Endings): brilliant violet aura; for a number of hours equal to the Exalt's Essence, all damage rolls by allies against foes within a radius of miles equal to her Essence have their unsoaked/minimum damage dice automatically converted into successes (soak still applies normally first); same enter/leave duration-lock rule as Mars and Jupiter.
cost: 10 motes, 1 permanent Essence, and 1 permanent Willpower per use (reflexive).
compatibility: Only a Chosen of the matching Maiden who meets the Essence-4 and all-five-colleges-at-3+ prerequisites; each Greater Sign supersedes and cannot be combined with that Maiden's Lesser Sign (anima banner).
notes: 'Greater Signs' section in full, printed p. 235/PDF 238, immediately after the House of Endings closes the Catalog of Colleges. This short section (a single page covering all five Greater Signs) is the last rules content of Chapter Six: Sidereal Astrology; Chapter Seven: Storytelling begins at printed p. 238/PDF 241 (confirmed by rendering pp. 236-238/PDF 239-241, which are a full-page illustration, a page of Chapter Six/Seven-transition fiction, and the 'Chapter Seven -- Storytelling' header itself) and is GM-advice/setting content outside this inventory's scope. This closes out the entire specific Colleges/constellations catalog task: all five houses (Journeys, Leisure, War, Secrets, Endings) and their 25 named colleges, plus this capstone Greater Signs mechanic, printed pp. 220-235/PDF 223-238.

name: Becoming the Wood Friend
summary: Terrestrial Circle spell that bonds the caster empathically to plant life, letting her move through dense foliage at full speed and become nearly untrackable until she next sleeps.
requirements: Prerequisite Charm: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery.
mechanics: Target: Caster. Until the caster next sleeps: she moves through even the densest foliage unhindered at top speed with no Athletics roll; forest, scrubland and cultivated fields count as open terrain for speed/fatigue purposes; no mundane tracking method can follow her (her scent becomes plant-like); supernatural trackers suffer a +2 difficulty to track her, and this sorcery overrides any Charm or effect that would otherwise make her easier to track. She adds her Essence to Strength for jumping/climbing through wooded terrain and to Dexterity for base movement speed in green environments, and adds Essence to other Athletics rolls made moving through or balancing on plant life. The bond runs both ways: the caster must succeed at a Willpower roll to knowingly do serious harm to a living plant or tree (cutting live wood, setting unprotected fires, joining a large-scale harvest); gathering fruit/nuts, collecting fallen wood, or pruning dead branches does not count. Committing such harm instantly ends the spell and locks the caster out of recasting it for three full days.
